newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Surging Nigerian shares edge higher.
newsitem.headline: Surging Nigerian shares edge higher.

text.p: Nigerian shares surged higher on Tuesday amid increasing interest in the market, traders said.
The all-share index stood at 7951.17 from Monday's 7951.19.
"Investors are showing healthy interest in shares despite sky-rocketing prices," said one dealer.
"They will remain in stocks for as long as money market rates are unattractively low," he added.
Regularly active shares were stronger as a result of the demand and, except for Industrial Gases which was adjusted for dividend and scrip, only one stock fell at the dealing session, traders said.
They added some shares previously experiencing negative movements reversed that trend on Tuesday.
Notable gainers included Ashaka Cement, rising 20 kobo to 13.60 naira as investors formerly selling the shares reconsidered their position.
"They felt it would be wise to hold than dump them for other stocks trading at much higher prices and with little possibility of paying better dividends," one broker said.
Guinness also strengthened by 30 kobo to close at 7.40 naira. Nigerian Breweries went 20 kobo up at 16.40 naira for similar reasons.
Food companies Nestle and Nigerian Bottling Company rose on long-running positive perception.
While Nestle finished 60 kobo more at 64.00 naira, the bottler was 50 up at 47.00 naira.
Close interest in banking shares saw the sector leader First Bank close 25 kobo up at 15.60 naira while UBA and Union Bank each rose 20 kobo to 11.50 naira and 13.45 naira, respectively.
Oil marketer Total appreciated by 30 kobo to 72.00 naira, the same as Agip which ended at 30.00 naira.
Unipetrol, the market's dearest stock at 74.25 naira was steady.
Niger Cement, the sole loser, fell two kobo to 68 kobo due to its unimpressive performance, said one dealer.
